problem: CoBuilder workflow state has no store. Slice states, scores, and attempts sit in the markdown tables of docs/plans/<slug>/04-slices.md, and any session can silently contradict that prose. Epic branches and pull-request numbers sit in hand-kept index joins. Nothing answers what is next, what blocks what, or what changed while two sessions worked one ladder.
why_now: Work runs locally, in cloud sessions, and with a team, so the backlog and the program states drift apart. The engineer wants no coupling of CoBuilder to beads, because Linear and Jira may follow. A layer between CoBuilder and the task system costs least before any caller exists.
approach: A tracker port in shared/tracker_port/ sits between CoBuilder and the task system. A neutral TrackerRecord and a TrackerPort carry every read and write, including sync, claim, and pull request operations. One projector turns records into data/index.json. Beads is the first adapter and keeps the metadata.cb envelope, with a proposed Dolt-in-git central store. A read-only files adapter and a fake adapter prove the seam, and one contract test runs against every adapter. Agents call one command, shared/tracker.py, and a shared reference teaches it.

alternatives.option: Keep markdown tables and hand-edited JSON as the only state
alternatives.rejected_because: State in prose races at whole-file grain, readiness is a human judgment, and nothing records who changed what.

alternatives.option: Sync the CoBuilder JSON and markdown files through git
alternatives.rejected_because: Concurrent sessions edit the same tables, so every sync gives complex merges, and no file records who moved a slice.

alternatives.option: Use beads only, and reach Jira or Linear through the bd bridges
alternatives.rejected_because: No bridge pushes metadata.cb. A Jira pull replaces the metadata column, and a Linear pull does so for a milestone issue. Beads stays mandatory.

alternatives.option: Call bd directly now, and extract the port at the second adapter
alternatives.rejected_because: Every caller holds bd calls, so the later extraction rewrites all of them. With no second implementation, the seam is a guess.

alternatives.option: Run an MCP server for each tracker
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-0016 says no plugin ships an MCP server. Scripts call a tool the way they call git and gh.

alternatives.option: Make each attempt its own record that relates to a slice
alternatives.rejected_because: No tracker has a child type for run history, and one issue per attempt clutters boards. The envelope keeps the latest score. Evidence files and comments keep the history.

alternatives.option: Store the same records in GitHub Issues or Projects
alternatives.rejected_because: Every flip needs network and credentials, offline work stops, and slice granularity would collapse into labels.

alternatives.option: Write a bespoke JSON or SQLite store for the bundle
alternatives.rejected_because: It rebuilds the engine beads already ships: readiness, dependencies, leases, history, and sync.

alternatives.option: Use beads milestone type for programs and avoid custom types
alternatives.rejected_because: Milestone fits the container half but not the stage workflow, and types.custom is the sanctioned path the queries want.

alternatives.option: Use one beads issue for each gate and each ADR
alternatives.rejected_because: Gates run in order on one program and block no other work. An ADR is a document with its own frontmatter. Scalar fields and a file pointer cost less.

alternatives.option: Copy the command table into each skill
alternatives.rejected_because: Four copies drift, and each tracker change needs four edits. One shared reference has one link in each skill, and a test checks each command that a document names.

out_of_scope: The Linear and Jira adapters. Each is a later program, tracker-linear or tracker-jira, and starts with a live-account smoke test
Moving prose documents, screenshots, or publication history into the tracker
The thread ledger in shared/ledger.py, which logs reply channels and holds no work-item state
Hindsight initiative pages, which stay separate
ADR issues. An ADR stays a file, and no decision issue exists
Options, review, and maintenance records. Every record that is not a program, epic, slice, or pull request stays a file
The gh:pr automation that closes a pull request issue on merge. A human closes it until that lands
Changing the viewer, the index shape, or any consumer key
Running the exported copy in a harness other than Claude Code. The export script copies shared/ and rewrites its paths, and no other harness has run it
risks: The port may take the shape of beads, because beads is the only real adapter. The capability flags and the contract test guard against it
Linear metadata takes only a string or a number, so a later adapter must encode a list of paths, for example as a JSON string
No tracker gives a verified atomic claim. When atomic_claim is false, a claim is a write followed by a read that confirms the claimant
The bd bridges do not push metadata.cb, and a Jira pull replaces it, so they cannot replace an adapter
Every state write needs a configured adapter. Without one, scripts read the file sources and refuse state writes
types.custom = program must ship in the tracker config, or the beads seed fails on a fresh clone
A cloud session that holds only a git clone may not run bd init and bd sync against refs/dolt/data. This is not verified
A pull request issue shows in bd ready until a human closes it, so every consumer must filter on metadata.cb.kind
A hand edit of a stateful line is overwritten from the tracker, and two sources of state exist until the generated file sections land
A gate that does not apply may store n/a. That is a leaning, not decided. A missing field means a gate not yet reached
A GitHub login names the claimant. Linear and Jira may resolve a login in a way that the user map cannot cover. This is not verified
An exported skill copy needs shared/ beside the skills and uv to run tracker.py. No harness other than Claude Code has run it
The shared reference and the four skills can drift apart. A docs test guards it: each named command must exist, and only the beads notes may name bd
testing: Run one contract test suite against every adapter. It checks that next_ready skips pull request and deferred items, and that it returns the right records for each kind and for under. When atomic_claim is false, it checks that claim_slice reads back the assignee. It also compares envelope values, runs the capability-gated paths, and blocks two epics with one pull request issue

Load the fake adapter from the checked-in fixtures in tests/fixtures/tracker/. They hold one program with gate scalars, three epics, three slices, and one pull request record. A golden index goes with them, and the projector test compares it value by value. A miniature docs/plans tree feeds the files adapter. No test reads the live repo's plans
Project a record list from the fake adapter and one from beads, and assert the same index. Project the files adapter alone against the current data/index.json, offline
Seed against a copy of the repo and compare projected counts against data/index.json
Round-trip one envelope through create, update, export, and list --json. Compare every value and every list item, and not only the keys
Close slice n and assert bd ready names slice n+1. Run next_ready with the file sources removed, and assert one call names the next slice
Assert that a write with no configured adapter fails, and that no script outside shared/tracker_port/ calls bd
Create one pull request issue that blocks two epics, and assert bd ready hides both until bd close
Write the gate scalars of Gates 1 to 4, 2b, and 4a to 4c on a program issue. Assert that bd show returns them unchanged
Run bd sync from a second clone and assert it sees the same programs, epics, and slices
Byte-compare the viewer index.html and assert that no goal.json epics[] carries branch, pr, or state
Run tracker.py over the fake adapter. Assert that stdout holds JSON, that a write with no adapter exits 2, and that bad arguments exit 4

Run tests/test_tracker_docs.py. The reference exists and four SKILL.md files name it. Each tracker.py operation in a document is a listed subcommand. Only the beads notes name bd. The reference is in AUTHORING_REFERENCES
reviewer_focus: The port: does any operation or record field only beads can serve, and could a capability flag replace it
The state vocabularies table: does every existing value land in a lifecycle or in the envelope without loss
The write model: does each command match a step that a session takes
The pull request issue: does its blocks edge match the moment a merge frees the epic
unknowns: Whether a cloud session that holds only a git clone can run bd init and bd sync against refs/dolt/data. The smoke check must pass before E2 closes
Whether bd claim is atomic. No test covers it
Jira: the claim race, the property limits, the create-time parent, a repeated issue create, and the rate limits
Linear: the claim race, a repeated issueCreate with the same id, and the sub-issue depth
Whether bd tree scales acceptably past a few thousand issues. The corpus is two hundred today
Whether a gate that does not apply stores the value n/a or leaves the field absent. The lean is the value n/a
When gh:pr automation closes the pull request issue on merge, in place of the human close
The name of the adapter config file. The proposal is .cobuilder/tracker.yaml
How Linear and Jira resolve a GitHub login to a user. The adapter config holds a user map
Whether a Linear or Jira adapter caches, and how. The later programs decide it
